youtube.aciklama: Bacterial meningitis is one of the most important acquired causes of severe permanent hearing loss. Inner ear inflammation can first fill the cochlea with connective tissue and then turn it to bone, called labyrinthitis ossificans; as it progresses, cochlear implant electrode insertion becomes harder. So hearing is tested without delay, and a child with severe loss is referred to the physician and the implant team.

cumleler: Why should hearing tests not wait after meningitis?
Bacterial meningitis is a leading acquired cause of severe permanent hearing loss.
Inner ear inflammation can first fill the cochlea with connective tissue.
This tissue can turn to bone, called labyrinthitis ossificans.
It can start within weeks and makes implant placement harder.
Test without delay; refer severe loss to the physician and implant team.
